test_title: RRB Technician Grade III Official Paper (Held On: 24 Dec, 2024 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: An athlete is moving with uniform speed in a circular track of radius R., and he completes one round in t s. The speed of the athlete is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For a **circular path**, distance covered in one round is the **circumference**.

**Speed** = **Distance** ÷ **Time**

Circumference = 2 × π × R

Speed = (2πR) ÷ t

**∴ The correct answer is (2πR)/t.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Radius of circular track = **R**

Time taken for one round = **t s**

**Formula Used:**

Speed (v) = Total Distance (s) ÷ Total Time (t)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/aa22ab5d9fc0fdfb494b3caaf4d49dd0c8af29b15c56fe5545168905df2b6113.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total distance covered in 1 round = Circumference of the track

⇒ s = 2 × π × R

⇒ Speed (v) = Distance ÷ Time

⇒ v = (2πR) / t

**∴ The correct answer is (2πR)/t.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Angular Speed (ω)

It is the rate of change of angular displacement, ω = 2π/t. Relation with linear speed is v = Rω.

Displacement in One Round

Since the athlete returns to the starting point, the **net displacement** after one complete round is **zero**.

Uniform Circular Motion

In this motion, the **speed** remains constant, but the **velocity** changes continuously due to the change in direction.</p
